title: Inside PostgreSQL
heroTitle: How PostgreSQL works, and where you can step in
heroLede: You are new here and want to contribute, so this guide explains the server the way a senior committer would in an interview. It follows one server from the Docker container and the files on disk, through the query engine and the write-ahead log, out to replicas and sharding. Every part has three diagrams, a walk through the real code, and the questions you would be asked.

how.title: Look
how.text: Start with the three diagrams. They show what connects to what.

how.title: Answer
how.text: Cover the answers and try every question out loud.

how.title: Open the file
how.text: Every path here exists in your clone. Open one after each part.

steps.name: Connect
steps.text: The client opens a socket. The postmaster forks a backend for it.

steps.name: Parse
steps.text: SQL text becomes a tree. Names are looked up in the catalogs.

steps.name: Rewrite
steps.text: Views are swapped for the queries behind them.

steps.name: Plan
steps.text: The planner guesses costs and picks the cheapest way to run it.

steps.name: Execute
steps.text: Plan nodes pull one row at a time from the scans up.

steps.name: Read and write
steps.text: Rows come from 8kB pages cached in shared buffers. Visibility rules decide which version you see.

steps.name: Commit
steps.text: The change is written to WAL first. Then the commit is durable.

callouts.title: Three ideas that explain most of Postgres

items.text: An UPDATE writes a new row version. Old versions stay until VACUUM removes them. That is how readers and writers avoid blocking each other.
Every change goes to the WAL before the data page. After a crash, the log is replayed. Replicas replay the same log.
Index types, table storage, functions, hooks and extensions all go through small tables of function pointers.

callouts.title: Honest answers to the questions people ask first

items.text: No. Core gives partitioning, foreign tables and replicas. Real sharding needs extensions such as Citus.

items.bold: Does it need special kernel permissions in Docker?
items.text: The server needs none. It refuses to run as root.
In 8kB pages inside files under one data directory.

tryItNote: Run these in a scratch folder. The checks were run against Homebrew PostgreSQL 16.

extraSections.title: Open work you can pick up
extraSections.lede: 37 tickets found on the pgsql-bugs list, the Commitfest app, the wiki TODO and in the source, each checked against git history and the mailing list. Scroll the table. Status changes daily, so reread the thread before you start.

table.caption: Difficulty runs from 1 (docs and tests) to 5 (deep core change).

extraSections.title: From reading to a first patch
extraSections.lede: PostgreSQL is learned best by building it, breaking it and reading other people's patches before writing your own.

footer: Built from a read of the PostgreSQL source, plus real runs against Homebrew PostgreSQL 16, then checked file by file by a second pass. Function names change between releases, so confirm against the branch you build.
